\[
H(f) = \max\left(0,\ 1 - \frac{\sigma^2}{P(f)}\right),\quad P(f) = \operatorname{mean}_{5 \times 5} \frac{|G(f)|^2}{N},\quad \sigma = 10
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(G\): The spectrum of the noisy image
- \(P\): The averaged power of G
- \(N\): The number of FFT samples
- \(\sigma\): The noise standard deviation

The Wiener filter for noise alone is H = S / (S + sigma^2), with S the power of the clean image at each frequency. White noise adds sigma^2 to the power at every frequency. So S is estimated as P - sigma^2, which gives H = 1 - sigma^2 / P, and 0 where P is below sigma^2. Here P is the power |G|^2 / N of the image extended with the border mode, with N the number of FFT samples. It is averaged over the 5 x 5 nearest frequencies to steady it. This estimate of S is this filter's own. The Wiener filter itself follows Gonzalez and Woods.
